claim: In the llmapper NBlood fork, -bot without -bot_visible (or -bot_realtime) draws no frame and runs the game clock as fast as it can; -bot_trajectory writes the player's x/y/z and sector once per game frame. The window is still made: launched hidden (bloodmap.oracle's SW_HIDE and CREATE_NO_WINDOW) and in the background, the run takes nothing from the desktop, and its per-frame sector is a better readout than any screenshot.
evidence: NBlood/source/blood/src/blood.cpp:2008 (bot Fast: totalclock = gNetFifoClock), :2066 (bDraw only when Visible), :1275/:1278 (flags)
bloodmap/oracle.py _hidden_process_options (STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW with SW_HIDE, CREATE_NO_WINDOW): nothing in the -bot path stops the SDL window being made
The owner, 2026-08-31: run NBlood 'only ... completely in background'. Said to the agent in conversation on 2026-08-31; not quoted in the repository.

blood.cpp:2008 and :2066 are in app_main; :1646 -bot_realtime clears Fast; llmapper/bot/bot.cpp:1592-1596 samples the trajectory once per gFrame; llmapper/bot/debug/bot_debug.cpp:159-166 sampleTrajectory writes tick, x, y, z, sector.
use: Run the engine only with -bot hidden, through a background process; read the trajectory.
